About this document

This document provides the teaching content for Science Year 11 of the New Zealand
Curriculum.
Progress and assessment information for Science Year 11 is still in development.
Once that is completed, Science Year 11 is proposed to be made by the Minister of
Education as a National Curriculum Statement under section 90(1)(a) of the
Education and Training Act 2020.
It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Science Year 11 will be required to start using it in Year 11 from 1 January
2028.
This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.

  In Science, students are taught fundamental concepts of physical and biological
  sciences, including matter, energy, environmental processes, and the interactions
  that shape the natural world. They are taught how biological systems function and
  sustain life, and how to investigate phenomena, gather evidence, and test
  theories.

Students are taught how science interacts with society, technology, and the
environment. Through Science, students learn how scientific knowledge is developed,
tested, and applied to explain the properties of materials, chemical, biological, and
physical processes, living systems, and Earth’s systems. They use evidence, models,
and scientific reasoning to understand natural phenomena, evaluate claims, and
make informed decisions about issues that affect people, society, and the
environment.
Science provides students with the knowledge and practices to test, represent and
communicate ideas, evaluate and synthesise information, analyse and apply
evidence, as well as know and understand scientific disciplinary knowledge.
As students progress through Year 11, they are taught to understand and use key
scientific concepts, terminology, principles, models, and frameworks that describe and
explain natural phenomena. They are also taught disciplinary knowledge that enables
them to evaluate scientific claims, explanations, methods, and applications using
evidence and scientific criteria.

  Science leads to pathways in science and related fields such as chemistry,
  biology, physics, Earth and space science, agriculture and horticulture science,
  the food and fibre industry, biomedical science and engineering, and a wide
  range of future study and career opportunities.

Scientific investigations
Scientific investigations involve students undertaking a more in-depth exploration of a
phenomenon or question. Investigations typically require students to pose or refine a
question, collect or source data, analyse evidence, identify patterns or relationships,
and draw evidence-based conclusions. Investigations will typically take one to two
lessons to complete.
At Year 11, investigations build on the investigative methods developed in Phases 1–
4. Investigations may involve experimentation, modelling, classification, or
investigating relationships between variables. Associated investigative skills include
observation, secondary source research, communication, responsible practice, and
repeated measurement.
Investigation requirements
At Year 11, schools are required to provide opportunities for students to undertake:
    •   at least one of either option A, B, C, D or E investigation provided within the
        teaching sequence, and
    •   at least two additional investigations from either the options (A to E), the
        examples provided, or school-designed.
